source_name: Advokatska kancelarija Duraković (Bar, ME) - local law firm with procurement practice
why_relevant: Example of the domestic law-firm layer that publishes practitioner commentary in Montenegrin on procurement procedures and remedies. Domestic-firm commentary is the sr-language counterpart to international guides and often flags bylaw-level problems earlier.

source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava — Stavovi / Prakse (legal positions and case practice)
why_relevant: Consolidated legal positions of the review body — shows how the Commission systematically treats recurring disputes (e.g. discriminatory technical specifications, references/qualification criteria, abnormally low bids), which predicts how future IT/payments tender challenges will resolve.

source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava — Aktuelnosti (news, sessions, work reports)
why_relevant: Where the Commission announces sessions and typically posts its periodic/annual work reports (izvještaj o radu) containing caseload statistics — number of appeals by procedure type, outcome split, which authorities are most challenged.

source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava — Pravni okvir (laws and secondary regulation)
why_relevant: Authoritative pointer to the Zakon o javnim nabavkama and implementing rulebooks that define thresholds, publication duties and appeal deadlines — needed to interpret what must be published and therefore what is collectable.

source_name: Izvještaji o javnim nabavkama u Crnoj Gori (annual national procurement reports)
why_relevant: The core aggregate market-sizing source for the cell: annual reports give total procurement value, number of procedures, split by procedure type and by subject/CPV category, and by contracting authority — the denominator for estimating the addressable IT/payments procurement market.

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija — Politika javnih nabavki (gov.me)
why_relevant: The ministry-level landing page for procurement policy on the central government portal; carries strategy documents, action plans, draft laws and public consultations. Often hosts newer report editions than the legacy ujn.gov.me site.

source_name: portalujn.gov.me — legacy public procurement portal (Delta 2015)
why_relevant: Legacy portal holding pre-CEJN notices and awards; useful for historical back-series of IT/payments tenders before the 2018+ e-procurement migration.

source_name: Upravni sud Crne Gore — Odluke (Administrative Court decisions)
why_relevant: The appellate layer above the procurement Commission: contested Commission decisions go to the Administrative Court within 20 days. Judgments restate the facts of the tender dispute and are the definitive outcome, and the Commission's own caseload includes cases returned on the basis of court judgments.

source_name: Institut alternativa — public administration and procurement oversight research
why_relevant: Montenegrin think tank producing structured monitoring of public administration reform and public finance, including analyses of procurement control and appeal mechanisms; useful for interpreting institutional capacity and reliability of the official statistics.

source_name: SIGMA (OECD/EU) — Public Administration in Montenegro monitoring reports
why_relevant: SIGMA scores Montenegro's public procurement and remedies system against EU principles, including explicit assessment of the review body's capacity, timeliness and decision quality — an external calibration of how much weight to place on Commission data.

source_name: MAPS — Assessment of Montenegro Public Procurement System 2024
why_relevant: Full methodological assessment of the Montenegrin procurement system, including remedies/appeals pillar and market-level spend analytics. The single densest English-language reference on how the system works, its data availability and its weaknesses.

source_name: European Commission — Montenegro Enlargement Report (Chapter 5: Public Procurement)
why_relevant: Annual EU assessment with a dedicated public-procurement chapter covering the remedies system, transparency of intergovernmental-agreement procurement, and reform trajectory. Sets the reform agenda that will shape future tender rules — including e-procurement and IT spending.

source_name: wapi.gov.me document delivery endpoint (government document CDN)
why_relevant: Montenegrin government PDFs — including Commission caseload documents surfaced in search results — are served from UUID-based wapi.gov.me URLs with no human-readable filename. Understanding this endpoint is a prerequisite for any reliable government-document harvesting pipeline in ME.

source_name: Montenegrin business press coverage of procurement appeals (e.g. Standard.co.me)
why_relevant: Domestic media report individual appeal outcomes with named bidders, disputed amounts and the intention to escalate to the Administrative Court — a low-latency signal that a contested award exists, often before the decision PDF is indexed.

source_name: Pošta Crne Gore — Javne nabavke (procurement page)
why_relevant: National postal operator is a sector contracting authority (postal services regime) AND a payments actor in its own right (counter payment transactions, Cash Express/Western Union/Ria/MoneyGram, card terminals at counters, CKB ATMs on premises). Its own procurement page carries simple-procurement outcome notices and signed contracts (ugovori) that do not always surface prominently on the central portal — including counter/IT/UPS/peripheral equipment relevant to self-service and cash-handling refresh cycles.

source_name: Pošta Crne Gore — Usluge novčanog poslovanja (money services page)
why_relevant: Not a tender source, but the authoritative description of what the post's counter payment estate actually does (domestic payment transactions, Cash Express, Post Cash, Western Union/Ria/MoneyGram, card terminals treated as cash advance, CKB ATMs sited in post offices). Reading it lets you interpret which procurement lots map to payments infrastructure and which partner banks are incumbent.

source_name: EPCG — Public Procurement (English mirror)
why_relevant: English-language mirror of EPCG procurement; useful for cross-language term mapping and for lots aimed at international suppliers.

source_name: CEDIS (Crnogorski elektrodistributivni sistem) — Javne nabavke / sitne javne nabavke
source_subtype: SOE / sector contracting authority procurement page
why_relevant: Distribution system operator; the buyer of metering (brojila) at scale — three 2022 meter tenders totalling roughly EUR 9.6m for ~30,000 meters were reported. Smart metering procurement is adjacent to payments (prepaid/remote billing, collection) and to the same field-device supplier pool. The 'sitne javne nabavke' (low-value) page is where smaller, faster-moving lots appear that never reach the central portal's headline feed.

source_name: Aerodromi Crne Gore — Javni pozivi
why_relevant: Airport operator is a sector contracting authority (airports). Directly payments-relevant: it runs public calls for leasing space at Podgorica and Tivat airports for the INSTALLATION OF ATMs (bankomati), i.e. it is the gatekeeper for airport ATM/FX estate — a recurring commercial opening for cash-handling and self-service players. Also runs equipment tenders (X-ray, lifts, fire vehicles) that show its procurement cadence.

source_name: Air Montenegro (ToMontenegro) — dedicated procurement subdomain
why_relevant: The Montenegro Airlines successor runs a SEPARATE procurement subdomain rather than publishing only centrally — exactly the actor-type blind spot this cell exists to cover. Publishes tender documentation as PDFs, including English-language versions. Payments relevance is indirect (card acceptance, onboard/ticketing payments, PSO route tenders) but the site is a clean, low-noise buyer feed.

source_name: Luka Bar AD — Tenderi i javne nabavke
source_subtype: SOE tender category feed (WordPress category, paginated)
why_relevant: Port of Bar is a sector contracting authority (sea ports) and a listed SOE. Publishes tenders, public calls for sale of assets, free-zone user selection and property leases in both Montenegrin and English. Useful as a buyer feed and as a barometer of SOE commercial activity; lease/free-zone calls occasionally cover on-site service points.

source_name: Monteput d.o.o. — road operator / electronic toll collection (ENP)
why_relevant: State road company operating the Sozina tunnel and highway tolls. This is a payments buyer in the truest sense: tolls are collected in cash, BY BANK CARD, and via electronic toll collection (ENP/TAG). It has tendered video/ANPR toll-collection equipment (award reported to Emovis) and runs the 'modeli naplate' payment-channel estate. A recurring buyer of payment terminals, cash handling at toll lanes, and TAG device distribution/top-up.

source_name: Fond za zdravstveno osiguranje Crne Gore (FZOCG) — Javne nabavke
why_relevant: Health insurance fund: a very large public buyer and a card issuer/administrator in its own right (health insurance cards, contracts with pharmacies and providers). Its site carries a javne nabavke section plus contract registers with providers — relevant to card personalisation, identification, and claims/settlement infrastructure.
